subject: Follow-up: Prompt samples, redaction guidance & eval next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lexicorp.com>, Tom Saunders <tsaunders@lexicorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Prompt samples, redaction guidance & eval next steps

Hi Elaine / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope a short eval: 

Recap
- Primary goal: improve customer-sentiment classification and guided-response suggestions inside LexiCorp Support Assistant.
- Key constraints: ~200ms average TTF (time-to-first-token) target for 1–2 turn interactions; strict PII redaction requirements (HIPAA-adjacent fields flagged); budget target ~ $Xk/month for pilot.

What we need from you (action items)
1) Sample prompts: please upload ~200 representative user prompts (CSV preferred) including: typical questions, escalations, and 10–15 edge-cases (example: multi-turn with code snippets, partial PHI). Label each row with "intent" if available.
2) Edge-case notes: flag any queries that must be redacted or routed to human agents.
3) Redaction preferences: Share examples of what you consider acceptable redaction (masked vs. tokenized) and any internal policies we should follow.

Attachments I’ve included: prompt sample template (lexi_sample_prompts.csv) and our redaction guidance PDF (redaction_guidance.pdf).

Proposed Redwood eval plan (high level)
- Models to benchmark: redwood/balanced-7b (low-latency baseline) and redwood/opt-13b-quant (quality/cost tradeoff).
- Metrics: classification accuracy, hallucination rate (manual spot-checks), TTF, cost per 1k tokens, and regression detection on the provided prompt set.
- Timeline: sample intake this week -> sandbox run by next Tue -> 3-day internal review -> 1-week pilot.

Links
- Eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLexiEval
- Benchmarks (example): https://app.redwood.ai/evals/bench/RDF-LEX-2028-0317

Next steps
- Can you drop the CSV in the Drive folder by EOD Monday? If you prefer, attach here and we’ll ingest.
- Let us know if the 200ms TTF constraint is firm — we can prioritize lower-latency variants for early tests.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15 min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: lexi_sample_prompts.csv (template), redaction_guidance.pdf (policy examples)

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@lexicorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Saunders <tsaunders@lexicorp.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt samples, redaction guidance & eval next steps

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear summary.

I’ve attached an initial export (lexi_sample_prompts.csv) with ~120 rows — we still need to run a quick PII sweep. A few notes:
- Several of our support transcripts include customer account numbers and some phone numbers — we can provide masked versions but would like guidance on what you recommend for the eval (mask vs. synthetic replacement).
- Edge-cases: I tagged ~12 rows as "sensitive" where we prefer human routing. See column "route" in the CSV.
- Timeline: internal procurement needs the SOW for review; can you share a one-page scope?

Questions for Redwood:
- Can the balanced-7b meet the 200ms TTF on your hosted tier or would we need Dedicated capacity for that SLA?
- For the hallucination metric — do you run automated checks or is that manual spot-checking?

Attached: lexi_sample_prompts.csv (initial), NDA already in place on file.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Prompt samples, redaction guidance & eval next steps

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Elaine's CSV and the notes. Key asks below; looping you for scoping and next steps.

Quick ask list
- Ben: procurement & pricing — can you sketch a pilot quote for a 4-week Dedicated trial vs hosted-with-priority for the RDF-LEX-2028-0317 deal? We need a one-page SOW for LexiCorp procurement.
- Marissa: Eval team — please run our standard model-fit bench on the attached 120-row CSV. Prioritize: redwood/balanced-7b (latency baseline) and redwood/opt-13b-quant (quality w/ quantized weights). Include:
  * Classification accuracy on labelled rows
  * Hallucination spot-check: sample 25 outputs manually and tag issues
  * TTF (P95) and cost per 1k tokens estimate
  * Flag any prompts that may leak PII (we'll redact/sanitize)

Also see: redaction_guidance.pdf attached — suggested masks and synthetic-sample rules. For the PII question: recommend synthetic replacement for names and token-mask for account numbers in the pilot; we'll document both so LexiCorp can choose at deployment.

If you want, I can schedule a 30-min tech sync with LexiCorp next week to align on redaction/labeling decisions.

Thanks — Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 18 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Prompt samples, redaction guidance & eval next steps

Neha / Marissa — thanks for the forward. I can get a one-page SOW and a pilot estimate together today. Quick notes:
- Pricing: Dedicated 4-week pilot (reserve small GPU pool) — rough ballpark $18k–$25k depending on burst capacity. Hosted priority lane option ~ $9k–$12k. I’ll spell out both in the SOW.
- Delivery: CS engineer (assigned) + 2-day bench run once we ingest the CSV.
- Next: I’ll attach a scope doc (lexi_poc_scope.docx) and a short checklist for procurement.

Marissa — once you have the bench results, can you include a short "regression risk" summary (are there prompt patterns where quality drops) and any guardrail recommendations? LexiCorp wants to limit false-positive escalations (human routing) to under 3% of interactions in pilot.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with files.

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: lex i_poc_scope.docx (SOW stub)
